title: 2010 HMMT February Guts Problem 21
statement: Let \(\triangle A B C\) be a scalene triangle. Let \(h_{a}\) be the locus of points \(P\) such that \(|P B-P C|=|A B-A C|\). Let \(h_{b}\) be the locus of points \(P\) such that \(|P C-P A|=|B C-B A|\). Let \(h_{c}\) be the locus of points \(P\) such that \(|P A-P B|=|C A-C B|\). In how many points do all of \(h_{a}, h_{b}\), and \(h_{c}\) concur?

solutions.text:
2 The idea is similar to the proof that the angle bisectors concur or that the perpendicular bisectors concur. Assume WLOG that \(B C>A B>C A\). Note that \(h_{a}\) and \(h_{b}\) are both hyperbolas. Therefore, \(h_{a}\) and \(h_{b}\) intersect in four points (each branch of \(h_{a}\) intersects exactly once with each branch of \(h_{b}\) ).
